page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The method
lines: Benzene is warmed with a nitrating
steps.why: Concentrated sulphuric acid is present to convert nitric acid into the nitronium ion, which is the species that replaces a hydrogen atom of the ring. The temperature limit is part of the method: at a higher temperature a second nitro group enters the ring and dinitrobenzene is formed.
common_mistakes: Using dilute nitric acid. Both acids of the nitrating mixture are concentrated.
Leaving out the concentrated sulphuric acid. It is half of the nitrating mixture.
Heating strongly. At a higher temperature, with more of the nitrating mixture, a second nitro group can enter the ring.
steps.memory_tip: Nitrating mixture is two concentrated acids, HNO₃ and H₂SO₄, kept below 60 °C.
steps.margin_note: Name both acids and give the temperature limit before writing the equation.

steps.label: The equation
steps.why: The displaced hydrogen atom and the –OH of the nitric acid leave together as water, so water is the second product here and not hydrogen chloride. Counting atoms, there are 6 C, 7 H, 1 N and 3 O on each side.
common_mistakes: Writing HCl as the second product. In nitration the second product is water.
Writing the product as C₆H₆NO₂. Benzene loses one hydrogen atom, so it is C₆H₅NO₂.
steps.memory_tip: The nitro group goes on and water comes off.
steps.margin_note: One closing line naming the product nitrobenzene completes the answer.

insider_note: Two details are easy to leave out of this short answer: that both acids are concentrated, and that the temperature is held below 60 °C. Write the equation with water as the second product, not hydrogen chloride.
